correctness.rationale: Circular binary t-window one-counts form an unbroken integer interval because successive windows change count by at most 1; the minimum and maximum each advance by 0 or 1 with length. Under μ all even positions are zero and odd positions complement the original; even windows sample m odd positions and odd windows sample r or r+1. The two odd-start parity intervals abut/overlap, giving the displayed minima and maxima and exact lengthwise a_w recurrences, even at r=0 and m=n. Summing odd lengths telescopes the L_w differences to |w|_1 and gives universal S transport. For P_k one-count q_k=(2^k−(−1)^k)/3 and the S recurrence solve to the closed form. Independent direct cyclic rolling-window profiles tested all 254 nonempty binary words lengths 1..7; complete universality is proven by the algebraic argument, not enumeration.

value.rationale: The arbitrary-input morphic transport identity and complete finite-circle lengthwise spectrum are a useful and reusable exact relation in combinatorics on words; the nontrivial summation of all cyclic Parikh classes is motivated by the classical period-doubling word, not an arbitrary numerical slice.

final_claim: For every nonempty binary circular word w with S(w)=Σ_{t=1}^{|w|}(max circular t-window ones−min+1), the period-doubling morphism μ(0)=01, μ(1)=00 transports the full lengthwise extrema by explicit even/odd formulas and satisfies S(μ(w))=2S(w)+|w|−|w|_1. Consequently S(μ^k(0))=((3k+10)2^k−(−1)^k)/9 for all k>=0, with an exact recursive spectrum at every rank and factor length.
